newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Rate on Yugo c.bank bonds down to 88.89 pct.
newsitem.headline: Rate on Yugo c.bank bonds down to 88.89 pct.

text.p: The National Bank of Yugoslavia (NBY) sharply cut an interest rate for its short-term bonds auctioned on Wednesday to an annual 88.89 percent, the Belgrade bourse reported.
This compares to an annual 147.48 percent rate set for its previous tranche of bonds auctioned on January 13.
The NBY auctioned a new 20 million dinar tranche of its 30-day bonds but sold 1.2 million dinars worth, the Belgrade bourse spokesman Milko Stimac told Reuters.
Traders said they were surprised at the NBY's move.
"We were prepared to buy more than 12 million dinars worth of bonds at a higher rate," a trader said.
"The only explanation is that the bank hoped to attract plenty of funds at a lower rate," the trader said.
The latest reduction of the bonds' rate also caught analysts by surprise.

"NBY has been playing with bond rates for sime time now. First they offer at 121.8 percent, then raise the rate to a record 147.48 percent and then suddenly cut it down so sharply. They seem not to want us to understand every move they make," said an analyst who asked not to be named.
There was no one at the central bank immediately available for comment. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
